asi.cache_semantics: key = relative path; value = (size, mtime_ns, result). Any write updates mtime so a stat match proves same content for all flows we control (event appends, receipts); shutil.copy2 preserves size+mtime so the staged copy reuses the source scan's per-file results; events.ndjson appended between scans only re-reads that one file. Stats taken AFTER read so fingerprint matches bytes actually read. Unreadable files never cached. Sensitive scan also populates the hash cache so the publishable digest after a scan hits per-file hashes instead of re-reading.
asi.hypothesis: per-file stat cache for _sensitive_candidates + _publishable_tree_digest: archive run scans same content 5x + digests 4x; cache per file instead of re-reading bytes each pass

description: inode-keyed sha256 cache shared across manifest/coverage/durable payload hash passes; benchmark switched to median-of-5

Tree digest byte format unchanged (bytes.fromhex) so old durable receipts still reconcile.

description: git_run memoization for hash-pinned read-only queries (dedup 22x rev-parse + 10x git archive per run)

description: result-memo for compute_product_tree_hash_for_commit (git archive 10x -> 1x per run; identity/resolution paths shared it)

asi.hypothesis: compute_product_tree_hash_for_commit called subprocess.run git archive directly (bypassing git_run's text-mode memo because tar output is binary); one execute resolved the same product commit 10 times -> 10 full tree extractions + tar parses + per-member hashing. Result-level memo keyed by (project, RESOLVED 40-hex commit, file_limit): a Git object tree is immutable so the result is deterministic; mutable inputs (HEAD, short hashes) resolve through rev-parse first so different resolutions never collide. Verified: git archive calls dropped 10 -> 1 per execute
asi.real_world_note: gain scales with repo size: each git archive on the user's real repos is a full product-tree tar extraction (Hunter-Harness ~600 files, CBM Forge larger); 10x -> 1x is seconds saved per archive on real projects. The tiny benchmark fixture (3 files) understates it

description: sensitive-scan regex fast path: pre-lowered subject + case-sensitive patterns + literal keyword probe (14x faster matching, proven byte-equivalent)

asi.ab_test: back-to-back A/B same window: WITHOUT median 7.18 (7.29/7.18/7.37/6.87/6.99), WITH median 7.05 (7.09/7.78/7.05/6.95/6.70). run_experiment window median 5.86 (5.76/5.85/5.86/5.89/5.89, spread 0.14s - calm system)
asi.finding: root cause found via isolation: the scan's cost was NOT I/O but the (?i) regex - Python re cannot use its literal-prefix fast path under IGNORECASE and falls back to per-position alternation matching, 14x slower on binary data (measured: (?i) search 1.122s vs case-sensitive 0.080s over the same 600x24KB files). sha256 over the same data: 0.008s
asi.hypothesis: regex fast path for the sensitive scan: pre-lower subject bytes (bytes.lower(): ASCII-only, length-preserving, C speed) + strip (?i) from the patterns (all-lowercase ASCII literals) + two-stage probe (pure literal keyword alternation as necessary condition; full patterns only on probe hit). Byte-for-byte equivalent to (?i) on bytes patterns because bytes-mode case folding is ASCII-only and offsets are preserved
asi.micro_evidence: warm-tree scan: ~1.15s -> 0.242s serial (regex portion eliminated); benchmark gain ~0.13s because the scan pool already parallelizes the regex work across 8 workers over only the first pass's real reads. Defender first-read tax on fresh fixture files (up to 8.5ms/file) dominates the benchmark's cold reads and is environment, not code
asi.verification: differential fuzz: 10000 cases across two seeds (mixed-case keyword injections, placeholders, internal recovery_token exemption, random binary) - 0 mismatches in match/no-match AND span positions; mixed-case PASSWORD= still detected; 44 runtime+preflight tests green; 215-test archive gate green via measure.sh; earlier 5 WORKER_IDENTITY_MISMATCH failures were traced to system load (Defender storm), not this change - verified by rerunning twice green with the change in place

description: opt-in stat-keyed events cache (load_events_cached): 17 -> 9 full parses per archive execute; benchmark-neutral, real-world 1.3MB log saves ~0.2s (scales linearly)

Linear scaling: ~0.8s saved on a 5MB log. The 9 remaining parses are semantically required (7 append_event loads after each append changes the file, plus first observation + post-freeze)
asi.hypothesis: events parse churn: one archive execute loaded the same events.ndjson 17 times (status gate, artifact preflight x4, collect x3, freeze, consistency, append_event x7). Added opt-in load_events_cached() in harness_events: per-process cache keyed by (path, size, mtime_ns) with double-stat torn-read guard; NDJSON appends always grow the file so the fingerprint can never hit stale bytes. Returns the SHARED list under an audited read-only contract - all 8 switched call sites in harness_archive verified read-only (append_with_auto_seal mutates only the new event; apply_event_corrections deepcopies before projecting; seal/phase-end helpers construct new dicts)

description: staging-copy hash transfer: before-manifest reads zero fresh files (copy2 kernel copy + source-side hash recorded per destination on stat match)

asi.ab_test: back-to-back A/B same window (v1 stream-copy attempt A/B'd first): WITHOUT median 6.37 (6.37/6.11/6.28/6.47/6.54), WITH median 6.08 (6.23/7.00/5.98/6.08/6.00). First attempt used a Python stream copy to hash while writing - it ATE the gain because shutil.copy2 on Windows uses the kernel CopyFile2 fast path; reworked to keep copy2 and hash the SOURCE instead
asi.corruption_equivalence: proven for every property checked today: pre-change, corruption during the staging copy itself was ALREADY undetected (before-manifest read the corrupted bytes from disk, cached them, after-manifest hit the cache -> before==after). Post-change records the source hash instead - equally undetected. Corruption AFTER the manifest (between before/after, freeze, collect) changes size/mtime -> transfer miss -> real read -> detected, unchanged. Durable staged readback and restore verification keep record_hashes=False and their real reads
asi.hypothesis: staging-copy hash transfer: the finalize staging copy of ~600 files was immediately followed by before-manifest reading all fresh copies back from disk (Defender first-read tax on every file). _parallel_copytree(record_hashes=True) now records (dst path, size, mtime, sha256-of-source) per copied file - copy2 preserves size+mtime so the destination fingerprint equals the source's, and the source hash is computed once during the copy. sha256_file consults the transfer map on a stat match. Opt-in: only the finalize staging copy records; durable/restore verification readbacks unchanged
asi.measured_effect: sha256_file call structure during execute: transfer hits 3031 / inode hits 640 / real reads 1244 (600 source-hash during copy [warm, near-free] + 600 durable staged readback [protocol-required] + misc). Both manifests + coverage now read zero fresh files. run_experiment median 5.55 (5.26/5.35/5.55/5.75/5.79)
asi.verification: 50-file differential: transfer hash == fresh disk hash for all; content-change after copy produces different hash (falsifiable); same-bytes rewrite falls through to real read; 193 archive tests green; bench integrity (before/after manifest reconciliation + durable readback) green
